A replacement asset must satisfy the applicable eligibility rules at acquisition and may not knowingly cause a prohibited concentration breach. ## 18. Defined Terms and Glossary

### 18.1 Core terms

Adjusted Collateral Principal Balance means the Collateral Principal Balance after adjustments required for defaults, discounts, low-rated assets and other specified items. Collateral Principal Balance means the principal amount of collateral recognized under the applicable definitions. Effective Date means December 15, 2026.

Reinvestment Period means the period ending June 20, 2029 during which Principal Proceeds may generally be reinvested. Non-call Period means the period ending October 20, 2027 during which ordinary optional redemption provisions are restricted.

### 18.2 Coverage and portfolio terms

OC means overcollateralization, generally the ratio of recognized collateral to relevant note balances. IC means interest coverage, comparing specified Interest Proceeds with required interest amounts. CCC Assets are obligations rated CCC/Caa or lower. Interest Proceeds are amounts characterized as interest. Principal Proceeds are amounts characterized as principal, including permitted sale proceeds and recoveries. WARF is Weighted Average Rating Factor; WAS is Weighted Average Spread; and WAL is Weighted Average Life.

Interest Diversion Test is the test that can redirect otherwise distributable subordinated interest into Principal Proceeds when the specified benchmark is not met. Measurement Date is a date on which the Calculation Agent determines compliance with a specified test.

## 19. Risk Factors

### 19.1 Credit and default risk

The collateral consists principally of below-investment-grade corporate obligations. Defaults, restructurings, downgrades and covenant breaches can reduce cash flow and collateral value. A portfolio recovery rate below the 52.5% assumption can increase losses to junior notes and subordinated interests and may trigger coverage-test diversions.

### 19.2 Recovery and concentration risk

Recovery depends on enterprise value, collateral ranking, documentation, competing creditors and market conditions. Concentration limits reduce but do not eliminate exposure to correlated defaults. Industry and geographic stress can cause multiple obligors to deteriorate simultaneously.

### 19.3 Interest-rate and reinvestment risk

Most collateral and notes are floating-rate, but their spreads, floors and reset conventions differ. Changes in Term SOFR can alter both asset income and note expense. During the 36-month Reinvestment Period, replacement assets may offer lower spreads, longer lives or weaker credit quality.

### 19.4 Liquidity and market-value risk

Loans may trade infrequently. The manager may be unable to sell an asset at a desired price or within the period required to cure a concentration or credit problem. Market-value declines can affect collateral tests even without realized defaults.

### 19.5 Counterparty and operational risk

Trustee, custodian, hedge-counterparty, administrator or account-bank failure could disrupt cash management. Operational errors in settlement, reporting or calculation may require correction and can create timing risk.

### 19.6 Structural, subordination and redemption risk

The notes are structurally subordinated according to their class priority. A coverage-test failure can divert cash from junior classes. Optional redemption or refinancing may repay notes earlier than expected, while market conditions may prevent refinancing and leave the securities outstanding longer.

### 19.7 Manager and regulatory risk

Performance depends partly on the manager's credit selection, trading and workout decisions. Regulatory, tax, accounting or capital-rule changes could affect transaction economics. Non-U.S.-dollar assets also create foreign-exchange and hedging risk.

## 6. Glossary of Transaction Terms

Adjusted Collateral Principal Balance: The aggregate principal balance of the portfolio, minus haircuts for defaulted assets, long-dated assets, and excess CCC/Caa assets.

Defaulted Obligation: Any asset for which the obligor is in bankruptcy or has failed to pay interest or principal for a period exceeding the relevant grace period.

Effective Date: The date (March 28, 2027) by which the Manager must have substantially invested the Target Portfolio balance.

Reinvestment Period: The period during which the Manager may buy and sell assets, ending on the Payment Date in October 2031.

WARF (Weighted Average Rating Factor): A measure of the default probability of the portfolio as assigned by the Rating Agencies.
